content: Dapsone is an antibiotic commonly used to treat acne. It works by reducing the number and severity of acne pimples and helps existing pimples heal more quickly. It is available in a topical gel form, often marketed under the brand name Aczone. How to Use: Before using dapsone gel, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Wash your hands thoroughly before and after applying the medication. Clean the affected skin gently with a mild or soap-free cleanser, then pat it dry. Apply a small amount of the gel (approximately the size of a pea) in a thin layer to the affected areas as directed by your doctor. Depending on the brand, this medication is typically used once or twice daily. Rub it in gently and avoid contact with the eyes. If the gel accidentally gets into your eyes, rinse them with plenty of water and contact your doctor if irritation persists. Use the medication consistently at the same time(s) each day to achieve the best results. Do not use more than the prescribed amount or apply it more frequently than directed. Side Effects: Common side effects of dapsone gel include skin redness, peeling, oiliness, or dryness. These effects are usually mild and temporary. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks. Serious allergic reactions to dapsone are rare. If you experience any unusual or severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately. This is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. Precautions: Before using dapsone, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, dapsone should only be used when clearly needed, as it passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Dapsone may interact with other medications, altering their effectiveness or increasing the risk of side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Using benzoyl peroxide alongside dapsone gel may temporarily discolor the skin (yellow or orange). Always consult your healthcare provider for advice on potential interactions. Overdose: If someone swallows dapsone gel and experiences severe symptoms such as fainting or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). For non-emergency cases, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. Storage: Store dapsone gel at room temperature and do not freeze it. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Notes: This summary does not include all possible information about dapsone gel. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
